Q1: Dodecylguanidine acetate exhibits known, significant hazards (Tier 1) for environmental impact, inhalation exposure, oral consumption, dermal and eye contact, and general organ/systemic effects, based on established GHS criteria. However, its potential for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR) and endocrine disruption (EDC) are currently considered data deficient (Tier 4), meaning comprehensive risk assessments for these areas are not yet possible.
Q2: Dodecylguanidine acetate is listed by the EPA as a "Pesticide Active Ingredient." This designation reflects its approved use in pesticide formulations, placing it on a specific list of regulated substances.
Q3: Dodecylguanidine acetate appears to be relatively well-characterized, possessing a clearly defined molecular formula and substance class, and it is not categorized as an incompletely defined (UVCB) substance. With 1,666 scientific references, it has been studied considerably more than many chemicals; however, specific data gaps persist regarding its potential for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity, and endocrine disruption.
